column3: The same فضل/رحمة conditional leaves mercy as the restraint on the otherwise unstated consequence.
Return before control, with repair implied by ch012/ch004, supplies a concrete limit on punitive consequence.
حكم and علم (b002/b003) frame wise judgment as equipped rather than merely punitive.
The matching conditional supplies the stated consequence that 24:10 leaves unspoken, across worldly and final horizons.
The opening of ch011 places 24:10 within imposed, clarified ayat rather than an isolated assurance.
Mercy and فضل are portrayed as preserving an entrusted gift; b004/b008/b009 support grace as sustaining provision.
Explanation, guidance, and return under علم/حكيم make tawbah an ordered opening rather than an exemption.
Its fixed penalty is boundary evidence: 24:10's فضل/رحمة does not dissolve the section's legal seriousness.
Clarification under علم/حكيم supports a bounded reading of the surrounding responses, through b002/b003.
فضل/رحمة interrupt a planned misguidance, while book and حكمة provide the protective discernment.
ch012/ch004 makes tawbah plus إصلاح the route by which wrongdoing's consequence is covered.
Its past-versus-future boundary is a secondary parallel: mercy does not erase a newly stated limit.
The removal of rage alongside selective tawbah offers only a broad, secondary restraint on retribution.
The section's relational prohibition gives 24:10 a disciplinary boundary without completing its omitted result.
Seeking forgiveness keeps the judging side answerable to mercy, a b004 corrective to unqualified condemnation.
Uncontrolled relay of fear or security is checked by referral and discernment; the same فضل/رحمة formula names the protection.
The fifth oath's curse marks the evidentiary limit immediately before 24:10's merciful closure.
Contrast route v12:tr:f-36_23-003 marks mercy amid harm as a boundary, not positive support for 24:10.
The repeated conditional connects فضل/رحمة with purification and resistance to a corrupting sequence.
Within ch011/ch012, tawbah and إصلاح explicitly qualify the preceding testimonial exclusion.
The invitation to tawbah and forgiveness is a secondary route from threat toward a still-open response.
علم/حكيم (b002) constrain response to betrayal; this supports measured judgment rather than automatic retaliation.
ch012/ch001 repeats the repair-qualified return pattern after a grave breach.
Mercy is requested together with prepared right direction, a secondary picture of enabling rather than mere pardon.
فضل belongs to Allah and is not controlled by a group; b008/b009 clarify its unowned bestowal.
The four-witness rule is the section's core evidentiary boundary for the mercy in 24:10.
فضل is bestowed by Allah; positive b008/b009 readings remain parallel to a contrary route marking non-entitlement.
Forgiveness and return lead to allotted good, while turning away retains the warning boundary.
Counter-testimony averts punishment, showing that the oath procedure itself can halt a consequence.
Intercession for those on earth and the forgiving/merciful names offer a broad secondary mercy frame.
Suspension between punishment and return under علم/حكيم preserves an unresolved consequence rather than presuming either side.
The refused tawbah after escalation is contrary boundary evidence for treating return as unconditional.
The merciful name is a compact parallel, but supplies no local mechanism for 24:10's halted clause.
It joins restraint of harmful speech with tawbah/mercy, supporting the social discipline around 24:10.
The fourfold self-testimony defines the procedural limit within which 24:10 arrives.
A positive b003 agency reading and contrary b002 route together keep human willing subordinate to wise determination.
حكيم/عليم gives only a general judgment frame; no direct mercy or return mechanism is supplied.
The opposing fifth oath completes the li'an boundary immediately before 24:10.
The same فضل/رحمة formula averts a named loss, a secondary analogue for the withheld consequence.
This statement about weakening hostile planning adds no clear local channel, branch, or mercy mechanism.
The required refusal to relay the allegation explains the conduct that 24:10's restraint protects.
Rahman's ordered creation is a broad secondary frame, not a route to the local conditional.
The final return to the Lord supplies no specific mercy, tawbah, or evidentiary contribution here.
ch012/ch003 joins tawbah, repair, grasping, and sincerity; it is a secondary structured-return parallel.
The merciful name after supplication is a general secondary resonance only.
فضل and نعمة under علم/حكيم carry several positive b002/b003/b008/b009 readings without selecting one.
The opening of the false-report passage assigns differentiated responsibility, framing 24:10's uncompleted consequence.
Selective return after conflict offers a secondary tawbah/mercy parallel without the local evidentiary setting.
عزيز/حكيم supports only a distant wise-authority frame.
The command to judge the report as manifest fabrication provides the immediate epistemic discipline for 24:10.
Mercy is explicitly contrasted with immediate reckoning, directly illuminating the deferred consequence in 24:10.
A prescribed release from oaths under علم/حكيم gives a secondary example of lawful relief rather than collapse of obligation.
The unmet four-witness demand identifies the speakers as false, the decisive proof boundary before 24:10.
Book-as-clarification amid disagreement, called guidance and mercy, supports an interpretive rather than arbitrary resolution.
فضل accompanies protection from harm after a response; it is a secondary preservation parallel.
No one else removes harm or repels فضل; ch005/b004 strongly locates relief and gift at their sole source.
Given فضل enables fitted capacity; b009 is positive while b008 remains a secondary mixed reading.
The command to ask from فضل, not envy allocations, contributes only a broad ethic of received gift.
The tongue-to-tongue relay without knowledge is the specific harmful chain whose outcome 24:10 leaves suspended.
Tawbah, إصلاح, and clarification together define return as reparative disclosure, not bare assertion.
Acceptance of tawbah and the name التواب الرحيم make return an active received response.
The condemnation of wishing indecency to spread supplies the social-harm boundary for 24:10.
Merciful authorization is paired with correct speech, a secondary boundary on who may speak and how.
Wrongdoers seek forgiveness and receive prophetic intercession; the result names Allah توابا رحيما.
Mercy accompanies a means of seeking فضل; ch009 supplies a secondary provision-and-care parallel.
Mercy as the purpose of sending is a broad positive b004 frame, without specifying the conditional's consequence.
Near return after wrongdoing is received under علم/حكيم, giving tawbah a timed and bounded shape.
The divine admonition never to return to the act turns the false-report episode toward a preventive future boundary.
The paired request for forgiveness and mercy is a direct but general supplicatory parallel, with mixed reading retained.
The presence of preservers suggests accountability but lacks a package route to mercy or tawbah here.
ch012/ch019 joins tawbah with righteous action, a secondary account of return becoming trustworthy action.
Mercy revives dead land through a staged process, a distant mixed analogy for restorative opening.
Return follows near deviation under the names ra'uf/rahim, strongly showing care without denying the deviation.
Seeking forgiveness and return culminate in merciful, loving relation; ch008 is a secondary repair route.
Revelation is named mercy so that warning may reach an unwarned people, a secondary communication frame.
Seeking فضل is permitted within guided remembrance, but offers no direct account of 24:10's mercy.
After the episode, holders of فضل are commanded to give, pardon, and overlook, enacting the mercy pattern socially.
Selective mercy and great فضل are a broad mixed parallel with no local return or proof procedure.
Repair is distinguished from corruption, while hardship is not willed; this supplies a secondary wise-limit frame.
Seeking forgiveness and return to the near, responsive Lord provides two ch012 branch routes without collapsing their distinction.
A promised request for forgiveness offers a direct but general b004 intercessory-return parallel.
The conditional prevention of corruption by counteraction is a secondary analogue for a withheld destructive outcome.
The later curse and great punishment for slander supply a firm boundary against reading 24:10 as immunity.
Entry into mercy through faithful giving is a secondary mixed route, not the local tawbah/proof mechanism.
After harm, tawbah and إصلاح require turning away from the pair; ch012/ch002 gives a concrete release pattern.
Against 17:87, possible removal of revelation marks the boundary that mercy and فضل preserve rather than possess.
Mercy is an exception alongside a completed judgment threat; it preserves the tension as boundary evidence.
A restrictive boundary is paired with promised فضل, a secondary example of provision beyond a closed channel.
Embodied testimony on the day of reckoning completes the accountability boundary after the local mercy formula.
The paired merciful names offer a foundational b004 frame but do not determine the omitted result.
The pairing of mighty and merciful keeps mercy from being read as absence of authoritative judgment.
Mercy is spread after despair, a restorative b004 parallel distinct from the legal setting of 24:10.
The night/day sign lacks a specific package channel, branch, or return contribution to 24:10.
Mercy and knowledge ground intercession for repentant followers and protection from punishment.
The bare call to taqwa and obedience offers no specific explanatory addition here.
The correction of an overclaimed state remains compatible with forgiveness and mercy, a b004 repair-oriented boundary.
Withdrawal and peace remove any sanctioned way against them, a secondary restraint on punitive action.
Mercy is self-prescribed, and wrongdoing followed by tawbah and إصلاح receives forgiveness and mercy.
Following the blessed book and taqwa toward mercy is a broad guidance parallel only.
Given حكمة begins with grateful recognition; b002/b003 offer a secondary disciplined-response frame.
The paired فضل and رحمة directly extend 24:10's two terms as received grounds of response.
Reliance on Allah after reform and warning is only a secondary limit-setting frame.
The local sequence turns to full recompense and manifest truth, preserving accountability after 24:10's mercy.
Its sorting language is a secondary boundary against treating the false-report passage as morally undifferentiated.
Permission before entry supplies ch016's controlled-permeability boundary against unregulated access.
Non-entry after refusal makes restraint and withdrawal an explicit procedural response.
The qualified exception for uninhabited spaces is a secondary boundary rather than blanket permission.
The command to lower gaze and guard chastity offers a broader preventive discipline for the section.
Its detailed privacy and adornment boundaries extend the section's protection of vulnerable interiors.
Ordered pairing and provision add a distant social-repair context, not a direct mercy mechanism.
The coercion clause ends with forgiving/merciful language, directly joining a violated boundary to mercy.
Clear ayat and an admonitory example support clarification as the section's response to confusion.
Claimed belief followed by turning away gives only a secondary contrast to trustworthy response.
Refusal to come for judgment when it is unwelcome marks the procedural boundary that 24:10 protects.
Readiness to submit only when right is expected exposes conditional compliance as contrary evidence.
The question of diseased, doubtful, or fearful hearts supplies a diagnostic boundary for refusal of judgment.
The believers' hearing and obedience gives the positive counterpart to the preceding evasions.
Obedience, taqwa, and fear establish a bounded successful response without canceling consequence.
Oath-making is checked by the demand for known obedience, a secondary evidentiary restraint.
Each party's responsibility under obedience reinforces differentiated accountability.
The promise to believers is a broad future-order frame, not a direct route through 24:10.
Prayer, zakah, and obedience name practices through which mercy is sought after the warning sequence.
The denial of escape supplies a final accountability boundary but no local repair mechanism.
The three permission times concretize ch016's protected-interior boundary.
Maturity changes the permission rule, preserving boundaries through changing circumstances.
The qualified concession for older women is boundary evidence because restraint remains declared better.
Enumerated no-blame cases distinguish lawful inclusion from prohibitive overreach.
Requesting leave from the Messenger formalizes bounded departure within collective affairs.
The warning against treating the Messenger's call casually guards response and accountability.
Complete knowledge of present states and return to Allah supplies the closing horizon of accountability.
Transgressing limits and its stated punishment are contrary boundary evidence against unconditional exemption.
The repeated warning formula adds no specific mercy, tawbah, or procedural connection to 24:10.
The test character of wealth and children is a broad caution, not a local account of فضل/رحمة.
A corrective release from self-imposed restriction gives a secondary example of lawful relief with forgiveness.
The call to turn back after hearts incline provides a secondary tawbah boundary without selecting an outcome.
Tawbah nasuh and the covering of faults directly extend 24:10's tawwab dimension with a future consequence horizon.
Allah's turning toward those left in distress makes tawbah an enabled return, not merely a human initiative.
The Messenger's ra'uf/rahim relation supplies a secondary care frame alongside the severe communal burden.
